newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asia Metals -- Japan zinc tight, demand brisk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Metals -- Japan zinc tight, demand brisk.

text.p: Japan"s physical zinc market continued to tighten, traders said, lifted by brisk demand from the construction and auto sectors.

They noted anecdotal evidence of buyers taking early delivery of zinc originally contracted for customs clearance on April 1 under Japan"s General System of Preferences (GSP), sacrificing the GSP scheme"s tariff exemption in order to get the metal more quickly.

One trader said consumer purchases of cars and homes ahead of the April 1 consumption tax hike had buoyed zinc demand from those sectors, while the yen"s weakness against the dollar had also lifted automobile exports.

While one trader said some zinc premiums had risen above $100 a tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices, another added that GSP-related imports from China, which account for a large share of Japan"s imports, were at fixed prices, so that the recent rise in LME prices resulted in lower premiums.
In the zinc concentrates market, sources at Australian mining house M.I.M. Holdings Ltd and Japan"s smelters said on Wednesday they had reached agreement on 1997 zinc treatment charges.
They declined to comment on the specifics of the deal, however, with a Japanese smelter source noting that further talks with other companies still remain.

Industry sources said the treatment charge was set at $170 a tonne based on an LME price of $1,000 a tonne, down $20 from last year and in line with a deal struck earlier this month between a European smelter and a Canadian mining company.
Another Australian metals group, Pasminco Ltd, said it is scheduled to hold talks with Japanese and South Korean smelters next week in Melbourne.

Aluminium traders this week began negotiations with producers on premiums for the April-June quarter, with several conceding that the Japanese would probably have to accept premiums in the $80 to $85 a tonne range, a $20 increase from the current quarter.
Japan"s premiums have firmed in line with higher premiums in the United States, while demand for aluminium, as with zinc, has been strong in Japan"s automobile and housing sectors.
They noted, however, that the jump in premiums had widened the gap between premiums paid by importers and those paid by major Japanese end-users, as traders competed to retain market share.

Japan"s copper market remained quiet, traders said, with little activity in imports. GSP-related buying was down this year due to the backwardation on the LME, while domestic smelters were producing flat-out as high treatment charges and the weakening yen boosted their margins.
